subject: MedAxis post-call: inference fit, latency/throughput SLOs & topology next steps
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@medaxis.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@medaxis.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call notes — inference fit & SLO constraints (MedAxis)

Priyom / Redwood team,

Thanks for the time today — useful call. Brief summary (please edit if I missed anything):

- Primary use case: clinical note summarization and physician query assistant inside our EHR. Data touches PHI; any hosted option must be HIPAA compatible or we need Private/on-prem.
- Performance targets: interactive UX for clinicians (P95 end-to-end latency target: <= 700 ms for typical 800–1200 token responses; goal is to keep token-generation latency P95 under ~400 ms where possible). Peak load: ~40–60 requests/sec during clinic hours, with traffic spikes to ~120 req/s for short bursts.
- Model needs: high-fidelity instruction-following, ~8k context, strict hallucination controls; we are open to a quantized 13B if accuracy checks out, but want a path to 70B later.
- Ops/security: audit logs, retained request/response traces for 90 days, customer-managed keys (KMS), VPC peering and egress control. SOC2 and HIPAA attestation required for procurement.
- Other constraints: low/no tolerance for downtime in production hours; fallback behavior if the primary model is unavailable (degraded quality acceptable but must remain online).

Immediate asks from our side: a short doc that maps Redwood deployment options to our requirements (latency/throughput sizing, data residency, EHR connectivity), and a proposed agenda for a technical deep-dive with your infra/engineers.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Kim
CTO, MedAxis

---

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@medaxis.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@medaxis.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call notes — inference fit & SLO constraints (MedAxis)

Hi Alex / Laura — thanks for the clear summary and for calling out the PHI + SOC2/HIPAA requirements up front. I captured the call notes and attached a short sizing worksheet and our privacy sheet. High-level recaps and clarifications below: 

1) SLOs & latency: we understand the interactive target: P95 end-to-end <= 700 ms. A few clarification questions that affect sizing: typical prompt size + expected average generated tokens per response (you mentioned ~1.2k tokens at peak, confirming?), and whether pre/post-processing (embedding/formatting) happens in your infra or ours.

2) Throughput & burst profile: peak sustained 40–60 req/s, bursts to ~120 req/s. That maps well to a Dedicated cluster configuration with autoscaling + burst reserve; for Private deployments we recommend keeping a small dedicated pool and enabling burst capacity into additional reserved nodes.

3) Model family & accuracy: we recommend starting with a 13B quantized variant for eval (reduced cost, faster latencies) and benchmarking hallucination rates. If you need 70B later, we can plan for a phased upgrade with canary rollout.

4) Topology options (brief):
  - Private VPC (recommended): Private control plane with customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and optional on-prem connector for air-gapped retrieval of EHR artifacts.
  - Dedicated (hosted in Redwood): Reserved H100 pool in your chosen region, strong isolation, Redwood-managed KMS option.
  - Hosted (not recommended for PHI): public-hosted API with business-associate agreement — still an option if you limit data sent.

Next steps I propose:
- Schedule a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive with our infra and runtime leads (Marissa + Aditya) to go through topology options, latency/throughput trade-offs, and a preliminary cost/size estimate.
- We'll share the attached: medaxis-postcall-notes-20270722.pdf and slo-sizing-estimate-20270722.xlsx.
- Please confirm whether a Private deployment (VPC + KMS) is a hard requirement for initial tests or if you can run a limited evaluation on Dedicated.

Proposed meeting slots (PDT): Mon 26 Jul 10:00–11:30, Tue 27 Jul 13:00–14:30, Wed 28 Jul 08:30–10:00. Tell us what works and we'll send an invite.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: medaxis-postcall-notes-20270722.pdf; slo-sizing-estimate-20270722.xlsx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@medaxis.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 20:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call notes — technical assumptions & questions (MedAxis)

Alex — quick follow-up from our runtime team after listening to the call recording and reviewing the initial numbers. I'm Marissa (solutions engineering). Below are technical assumptions and open questions that will shape the deep-dive topology and sizing: 

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Avg tokens per request: prompt 400 tokens + generation 1,200 tokens = ~1.6k tokens total per request; if generation is lower, latency and cost improve materially.
- Target model at launch: 13B quantized (fp16 → 8-bit Q8_0) for latency cost trade-offs; fallback path to 70B dense if accuracy is insufficient.
- KV cache usage: high — many requests will reuse patient-specific context (EHR note prefixes). We'll want prefix/KV caching on the gateway to reduce repeated compute.

Sizing notes (very preliminary):
- For 50 req/s sustained with 1.6k tokens/request and a 13B quantized model, a 3–4 GPU H100 dedicated worker pool with batching tuned to 20–40ms scheduling windows should meet P95 token-generation latency targets (model at 8k context window).
- For private VPC deployments, we recommend 2 head nodes (control plane) + 3 workers to start; burst capacity can be met by autoscaling into reserved standby workers. Exact numbers depend on average batchability and token distributions.

Security/compliance items to confirm:
- KMS: do you require CMK in your AWS account, or is Redwood-managed KMS acceptable for evaluation?
- Audit logs/retention: 90-day retention confirmed? Are specific fields required for regulatory audit (full request/response vs. redacted metadata)?

Questions for MedAxis to answer before deep-dive: 
1) Please share a small sample prompt/response (anonymized) or token count histogram if available.
2) Any network constraints: egress IP allowlists, NAT, or strict egress blocking?
3) Timeline: procurement window and must-have dates for production cutover.

I'll prepare a short topology sketch and attach a privacy/security one-pager (redwood-privacy-sheets.pdf). Priyom, if we confirm the slot, I'll bring our runtime tech lead and a deployment architect.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-privacy-sheets.pdf)
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@medaxis.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call notes — inference fit & SLO constraints (MedAxis)

Thanks Priyom / Marissa — this is very helpful and aligned with what we expected. Quick answers: 
- Average tokens: earlier estimate was high; realistic average is prompt ~350 tokens, generation ~800 tokens (so ~1.15k total). We'll extract token histograms and share before the deep-dive.
- Private VPC is a hard requirement for any production test with PHI. For proof-of-concept we can consider a dedicated, isolated cluster in your hosted offering if it's enclosed within our VPC via peering and KMS in our account.
- KMS: we require customer-managed CMK in our AWS account for production; for an initial eval we can permit Redwood-managed keys if data is pseudonymized.
- Audit retention: 90 days is fine; we will confirm whether full responses must be retained or redacted.
- Timeline: procurement/IPP sign-off desired by end of Q3; pilot start ideally mid-September.

Meeting slot: Tue 27 Jul 13:00–14:30 PDT works for our infra lead (Laura) and me. Please send a calendar invite and include a short agenda.

Best,
Alex
